subject: general
question: An object of mass 12 kg is located such that its potential energy relative to the ground is 480 J. Assuming g = 10 { m s}⁻² , what is the height (h) of the object?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gravitational Potential Energy (PE)** of an object raised to a certain height is given by the formula: **PE = m × g × h**, where **m** is the **mass**, **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, and **h** is the **height**.
 
• In this specific problem, the **mass (m)** of the object is **12 kg**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is provided as **10 m/s²**.
 
• The **Potential Energy (PE)** relative to the ground is **480 J** (Joules).
 
• To find the **height (h)**, we rearrange the formula: **h = PE / (m × g)**.
 
• By substituting the given values: **h = 480 / (12 × 10)**.
 
• Calculating the denominator: **12 × 10 = 120**.
 
• Final calculation: **h = 480 / 120 = 4**.
 
• Therefore, the object is located at a **height** of **4 m** above the ground. ***Hence, the correct answer is 4 m.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Potential Energy**: This is the energy possessed by an object by virtue of its **position** or **configuration**. In the context of gravity, it represents the **work done** against gravity to lift an object to a specific **height**.
 
• **Mass (m)**: It is a measure of the amount of matter in an object, usually measured in **kilograms (kg)**. In this problem, it is **12 kg**.
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g)**: On the surface of the **Earth**, the standard value of **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**, but for simplicity in competitive exams and school level physics, it is often taken as **10 m/s²**.
 
• **Joule (J)**: This is the **SI unit** of **energy** and **work**. One **Joule** is defined as the work done when a force of **one Newton** displaces an object by **one meter**.
 
• **Work-Energy Theorem**: The change in the **potential energy** of an object is equal to the **work done** by the external force in moving the object from the ground to that **height** without changing its **kinetic energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reference Level**: Potential energy is always measured relative to a **reference point**, which in most basic physics problems is the **ground** (where **h = 0**).
 
• **Energy Conversion**: If the object of **12 kg** were allowed to fall from **4 m**, its **Potential Energy** would gradually convert into **Kinetic Energy (KE)**. Just before hitting the ground, its **KE** would be equal to the initial **PE** of **480 J**, assuming no **air resistance**.
 
• **Scalar Quantity**: Energy is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has **magnitude** but no **direction**. This distinguishes it from **force** or **velocity**, which are **vector quantities**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The dimensional formula for **Potential Energy** is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is the same as that for **work** and **torque**.
